title: Reader Chapter 4
hook: A reader-facing chapter under phase-1 review.

breakdown.fullRead: A forecast gets safer when it moves between two distances. From far away, similar cases show the rough odds. From close up, people and small details show what the choice will ask of daily life. Either lens alone can mislead. Daniel Kahneman's curriculum team had an inside story that made sense. They knew the work, the talent in the room, and the steps on the plan. Then comparable projects pointed to a much longer timeline. The outside view was not smarter because it knew the people better. It was smarter because it had seen more cases. Ask experts for the kind of answer they are best placed to give. A seasoned operator may be weak at naming your one true future, but strong at naming a reference class. How long do projects like this usually take? How often do restaurants like this one make it? What happens when teams with similar plans hit the same wall? Close-up stories warm the average without letting it drive alone. Brian Zikmund-Fisher did not need only medical odds before transplant treatment. He needed to hear what patients lived through: the fatigue, the fear, the dull practical parts of recovery. The odds mattered. The lived detail mattered too. The skill is not picking numbers over stories. The skill is making each lens do its own job.
